sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Poverty is negated only by a wealth beyond filling lack, not by mere sufficiency, and lower daat leaves a hidden lack in the person because his consciousness of G-d is an addition to his own existence.

translations.translation: And according to what was explained above in section 4, that the negation of poverty
(lack)
is specifically through the wealth that is above filling the lack,
but not when the flow is only enough for his lack
[including also the matter of "that which he lacks"—
even a horse to ride upon and a servant to run before him]
there remains
(in inwardness)
a lack also regarding the contracted flow,
it must be said,
that even when the service is from the aspect of daat,
recognition and feeling,
but only lower daat that receives from Arich,
the service is like something additional upon him,
and the person himself
(in his inwardness)
lacks the service,
meaning that there remains a place in the person where the revelation of G-dliness does not shine.
For although the matter of recognition and feeling
(even of lower daat)
is that the person himself recognizes and feels
(as above in section 3),
nevertheless,
since the essence of the person is existence
(and not that his essence is the feeling of G-dliness),
his recognition and feeling of G-dliness is like something additional upon him.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Lower daat itself grants place to existence outside G-d, whereas upper daat from Atik, the Essence of Ein Sof, reveals that G-d's true existence is the true existence of all beings, filling all lack.

translations.translation: And on a deeper level it may be said,
that this—that in the service of lower daat a lack still remains—
is not only because the person and his recognition of G-dliness are two things,
but also from the aspect of the recognition itself
(the recognition of lower daat)
there is a granting of place to an existence outside of G-dliness.
For since lower daat receives from the externality of Keter,
Arich,
which in general is the aspect of Sovev that is like a source for worlds,
therefore,
even from the aspect of daat itself there is a granting of place to existence.
And this itself is the reason that through the revelation of this level in the person, he remains in his existence,
an existence outside of G-dliness.
And in order for the lack to be completely filled,
that is, that there be no place where the revelation of G-dliness does not shine,
it is through the service of upper daat that receives from the inwardness of Keter,
Atik,
which in general is the Essence of Ein Sof.
For regarding the Essence of Ein Sof, there is no existence outside of Him,
and on the contrary,
His true existence is the true existence of all beings.
Therefore, through the revelation of upper daat,
the person's recognition of G-dliness is in a manner that this
(the recognition of G-dliness)
is his entire existence.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Moshe's prayer to fill Knesset Yisrael's lack is called a rich man's prayer because from the perspective of upper daat, even their lack is not a lack, and his prayer was that this truth be revealed to them.

translations.translation: And based on this, we may explain why Moshe's prayer to fill the lack of Knesset Yisrael is called a rich man's prayer,
even though the lack of Knesset Yisrael certainly affected him greatly,
for Moshe is the aspect of upper daat
(as above),
and from the perspective of upper daat,
the matter of wealth,
the matter of lack does not apply.
That is,
in addition to the fact that in Moshe himself no lack applies, G-d forbid,
rather, regarding Moshe,
even the lack of Knesset Yisrael for whom he prayed is not a lack,
for upper daat receives from Atik,
and therefore it is felt in him that His true existence is the true existence of all beings and they lack nothing.
And although Moshe prayed for them,
and the matter of prayer is to fill the lack—it may be said,
that his prayer was that this matter
(that the truth is that they lack nothing)
be felt in revelation also by them.
But in Moshe this was felt
(that they lack nothing)
in revelation even when they were in a state that required him to pray for them,
and therefore,
his prayer is a rich man's prayer.
And to add,
that this—that Moshe's prayer is called a rich man's prayer—is not only because even then
(at the time of prayer)
he was rich,
but moreover,
his prayer was because he is rich.
For Moshe's prayer that the lack of Knesset Yisrael be filled
[Knesset Yisrael simply,
and through this—the lack of Malchus,
and of the world]
is that the lack be completely filled,
that there be no place where the revelation of G-dliness does not shine,
and in order for the lack to be completely filled, it is specifically through the revelation of upper daat,
as above.
